item.text:
**Bottom Line**  
5B.10 is mixed but overall slightly negative for a broad “stronger trajectory” reading. Compared with the inherited baseline, Tshisekedi’s 2024 team did preserve macro stability better than many conflict states could: the IMF saw reserve accumulation, revenue mobilization, and resilient growth. But the year still ended with high vulnerability, weak reform depth, conflict-driven spending pressure, and no clear evidence that the economy was left on a decisively stronger, more durable path than it started.

**Accepted Claims**
- **2024 Article IV Consultation, Sixth Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement** — IMF, 2024-07-15, https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/07/15/democratic-republic-of-the-congo-2024-article-iv-consultation-sixth-review-under-the-551892  
  - Claim: The IMF said the economy remained resilient, reserves kept rising, inflation was easing, and the program was broadly on track, but also that fiscal slippage came from conflict-linked spending and reforms were still slow. This is the strongest evidence that Tshisekedi left a somewhat steadier macro setup than he inherited, though not a transformed one.  
  - IDs: `5B.10`, `5B.9`, `5B.3`

- **Selected Issues: Democratic Republic of the Congo** — IMF, 2024-07-15, https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/07/15/democratic-republic-of-the-congo-selected-issues-551897  
  - Claim: Revenue mobilization improved, including around mining, but the state still had weak tax capacity and shallow fiscal foundations. This supports a modest improvement in trajectory, but also shows the improvement was incomplete and fragile.  
  - IDs: `5B.10`, `5B.3`, `5B.5`

- **Macro Poverty Outlook for Congo, Democratic Republic of: April 2024** — World Bank, 2024-04-03, https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099434404082425237  
  - Claim: The World Bank said terms-of-trade deterioration, higher imports, deficits, currency pressure, and inflation were still weighing on the economy, and that growth and poverty reduction remained vulnerable to commodity and geopolitical shocks. This is the clearest counterweight to any claim of a clearly stronger trajectory.  
  - IDs: `5B.10`, `5B.9`, `5B.3`

- **Discours sur l’État de la nation 2024** — Présidence RDC, 2024-12-12, https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/discours_sur_l_etat_de_la_nation_2024_le_chef_de_l_etat_dresse_un_bilan_porteur_despoir  
  - Claim: Tshisekedi said reserves had reached about $6.12 billion and the exchange rate had stabilized, presenting the year as a macro-stabilization success. This is favorable, but it is self-reported and weaker than the IMF and World Bank evidence.  
  - IDs: `5B.10`, `5B.3`

- **Democratic Republic of the Congo: Expanding and Equipping Primary School Classrooms for Better Learning Outcomes** — World Bank, 2024-02-28, https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/02/28/democratic-republic-of-congo-afe-expanding-and-equipping-primary-school-classrooms-for-better-learning-outcomes  
  - Claim: The new education project aimed at equitable access for girls and students with disabilities, but the same reporting showed overcrowding, missing materials, weak staffing, and poor water/sanitation. That suggests some forward motion, yet not enough to show a broad productivity trajectory clearly improved in 2024.  
  - IDs: `5B.10`, `5B.8`, `5B.6`

- **DRC: President Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis** — Amnesty International, 2024-06-24, https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/  
  - Claim: Amnesty said public resources were being squandered, essential services were underfunded, and mining expansion was driving evictions and pollution. That points to a weak overall development trajectory despite macro stabilization.  
  - IDs: `5B.10`, `5B.8`, `5B.5`, `5B.6`

- **Congo election commission overspent, awarded opaque contracts: report** — Reuters, 2024-01-15, https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report-2024-01-15/  
  - Claim: A civil-society report said CENI could not account for about $400 million and used opaque procurement. This is indirect, but it supports the view that the inherited governance environment still undercut a durable improvement in economic trajectory.  
  - IDs: `5B.10`, `5B.5`, `5B.9`

- **Army disarray hobbles Congo’s fight with Rwanda-backed rebels, officers say** — Reuters, 2024-07-17, https://theprint.in/world/army-disarray-hobbles-congos-fight-with-rwanda-backed-rebels-officers-say/2160048/  
  - Claim: Officers described mismanagement, weak logistics, demoralized troops, and proxy dependence. Even with some attempted correction, the security environment remained a major drag on any stronger economic path.  
  - IDs: `5B.10`, `5B.9`, `5B.7`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find a direct 2024 source that cleanly quantifies whether Tshisekedi left the economy on a stronger trajectory than the one he inherited after adjusting for war, commodity volatility, and external shocks.
- The evidence is mostly indirect and macro-level: IMF and World Bank assessments, plus self-reporting from the presidency. There is little hard evidence on employment, poverty reduction, or durable structural gains by year-end.
